title: Integrate weight-only INT8 quant profiles into CI regression and calibration harness
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Deliver a reproducible integration path for weight-only INT8 quantization profiles (GPTQ and AWQ variants) into Redwood's CI/regression pipeline and calibration workflows. Scope includes: a profile abstraction that the runtime and calibration tooling can consume; deterministic calibration dataset selection and seed handling; regression tests (smoke and golden) that assert accuracy and generation stability; and CI gating that prevents accidental accuracy regressions from merging. This ticket focuses on engineering integration and test automation rather than algorithmic research.
acceptance_criteria: 1) A profile abstraction that can represent layer-wise scales, zero points (if needed), and metadata for GPTQ and AWQ, stored in the quant_profiles bucket. 2) Calibration job in CI that runs on a small representative subset (<=100 examples) and outputs calibration artifacts deterministically. 3) Regression pipeline with a smoke test and a golden-eval set; PRs that change quantization code fail CI if top-level accuracy drops beyond defined thresholds. 4) Test harness documents exact seed and hardware used; results logged to the quant-dashboard. 5) End-to-end example with a 7B model demonstrating <=1.5% absolute drop on ROUGE-L for our chat-eval set (or configurable per-model thresholds).
tasks: Design profile JSON schema and storage location
Implement profile loader in runtime (C++/Rust module) with compatibility checks
Extend calibration tool to emit profile artifacts for both GPTQ and AWQ flows
Create CI job definitions (short/long) in .github/workflows that run on test runners
Add regression assertions to test harness and integrate with quant-dashboard
Write migration/compatibility converter for older quant formats
notes: Trade-offs: AWQ gives better accuracy for some models at the cost of slightly larger profile metadata; GPTQ is faster and more compact. We'll support both via a 'variant' field in the profile and runtime-selection policy.
Calibration dataset: use curated 100-example seed set from datasets/quant_calibration/seedset_v2. This is intentionally small for CI speed but representative across token lengths and domains.
Determinism: calibration must pin RNG seeds and use fixed CPU/GPU kernel ordering when running in CI. Use CALIB_SEED env var and runtime flag --force-deterministic-kernel-order.
Storage: write profiles to s3://redwood-quant-profiles/{model}/{variant}/{commit}.json with metadata header including git_sha, ci_run_id, and hardware_tag.

Fallbacks: runtime will fall back to a higher-precision profile or hosted model if profile validation fails; this behaviour is already supported by smart routing but needs explicit tests for quant-profile failures.
Performance note: weight-only INT8 introduction requires a small KV cache memory check — ensure the runtime refuses to enable quant-mode if tensor memory alignment is incompatible.
test_plan: Two-tier CI: (1) fast-smoke in PRs — run calibration on seedset_v2 (100 examples), apply profile, run 20-generation warmup and compare logits/top-k distributions; (2) nightly extended regression — run full golden-eval (1k examples) across 3 representative models (7B, 13B, 70B-int8 simulated) and publish results to quant-dashboard. CI must check: accuracy metrics, generation-length latency change (<20% increase), and memory stability (no OOM).
regression_thresholds: For PR-gate smoke: no >1.5% absolute drop in primary accuracy metric for each model. For nightly: alerts at >1.0% drop (high priority), and automatic rollback candidate if >2.0% drop across two consecutive runs.
final_decision: Support both GPTQ and AWQ profiles via unified schema. CI gate will block merges when deterministic smoke tests indicate an accuracy regression beyond thresholds. Nightly jobs will feed failure signals to the oncall and create automated incident notes if regressions persist.
